invariants.name: An ok line for the Codex hooks means that Codex runs each astack hook
An ok line for the Codex hooks needs a hooks/list reply
With a reply, doctor says ok exactly when the hook is on and trusted or managed

carrier.contract: The command gathers one Snapshot from the config files, codex app-server and gh, and maps it to one list of findings. An ok line for the Codex hooks needs a hooks/list reply that marks each astack hook on and trusted or managed.

category.equality: Two reads are equal when their kind and their hook list or cause are equal. Two finding lists are equal when their area, level and text are equal in order.

abstraction.hides: The JSON-RPC exchange with codex app-server, its deadline and the parse of the hooks/list reply, the gh reads of each base, and the parse of the review profile.
callersKnow: An ok line for the Codex hooks means that Codex reported each astack hook on and trusted or managed.
With no hooks/list reply, doctor warns with the cause and prints no ok line for the hooks.
A drifted review profile fails with each problem and its repair, and astack check hardening-profile prints the same text.
A base with no blocking rule gives a note and no FAIL.
Doctor writes only its skip file, its runtime file and the state that codex app-server keeps in CODEX_HOME.
abstraction.deletionTest: Deleting readCodexHooks puts the JSON-RPC exchange in doctor and in the dist check, so the two readers drift apart. Deleting diagnose puts each rule in the command, and the tests then need a real home folder for each case.

alternatives.name: Pin the content hash too
alternatives.rejectedBecause: Only Codex computes it, and it changes in each release.

alternatives.name: FAIL on each status other than trusted
alternatives.rejectedBecause: It fails a managed hook and passes a disabled one.

alternatives.name: Read hooks/list in a temporary CODEX_HOME
alternatives.rejectedBecause: That home cannot see the trust of the owner.

omitted: The model has one hook. The code applies the same rule to each of the 4 astack hooks, and the tests examine that rule.
The model takes the status that Codex reports as a true observation of the trust that Codex enforces.
The review profile rules and their YAML parse, the base note, the skip file, the version, the managed exit codes and the watch-pr clamp have no model state. Their tests examine them.

bounds: One hook, 3 releases with a new content hash each, and a managed flag that the start state picks.
Each order of the release, trust, toggle, read and report steps, with a read that can fail.

negative.defect: A doctor that reads only the trusted hook hash prints ok after a release, when Codex marks the hook modified and skips it.

limits: The finite model takes the Codex status as a true observation and covers one hook only.
The model does not show that the TypeScript code refines it. The linked controls and review examine that relation.
The recorded hooks/list reply comes from codex-cli 0.171.0. A later reply shape needs a new recording.
Exact-head CI, review, Shipping and every ordinary gate stay required.
